body.statement: Uniformly over \(\beta\in\mathcal K\) and balanced sequences with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), \[d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-(N/n)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)=A(\beta)\frac{m}{n^2}+o\!\left(\frac{m}{n^2}+\frac{1}{nm}\right),\] where \(A\) is continuous and \(0<\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}A(\beta)\le\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}A(\beta)<\infty\).
body.justification: This term prices the irreversible loss from assigning pilot units before the oracle geometry is learned.
body.gap: Han and Deng establish first-order equivalence after sample splitting but do not retain the deletion contrast at order \(m/n^2\).
body.consumer: It lets a replication planner quantify the marginal precision price of adding pilot batches.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform second-order one-wave oracle-gain or deletion-stability expansion strong enough to leave no term at the pilot-frontier scale.
obligation.obstruction: First-order finite-population Gaussian convergence gives only a little-oh remainder relative to one over the wave size. At the square-root pilot scale the theorem needs cancellation or a refined order-two expansion, including exact boundary ties and unequal Horvitz--Thompson inclusions; no frozen node supplies it.
obligation.attempted: Centered at the empirical oracle and Taylor-expanded the random-complement empirical moments. This closes the subset algebra conditional on an order-two one-wave expansion, but that finite-randomization expansion remains unproved.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact accounting theorem reduces this node to a one-wave expansion.  If one establishes, uniformly on regular subsets,
\[
d_T(\beta)=\frac{A(\beta,M_T)}{|T|}+O(|T|^{-2}),
\]
where \(M_T\) is the finite vector of empirical moments and \(A(\beta,\cdot)\) has two bounded derivatives, then uniform-subset identities give \(E(M_T-M_n)=0\) and \(E\|M_T-M_n\|^2=O\{m/(nN)\}\).  Taylor expansion then yields
\[
d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}
=A(\beta,M_n)\frac{m}{n^2}+O\!\left(\frac{m}{n^3}+\frac1{n^2}\right),
\]
which has the required remainder on the interior pilot scale.  The missing part is the uniform finite-randomization expansion for \(d_T\).
